planned_outcome: Land HMS Bellona: implement Zurcher 2014 two-state bread-baking model with radiative outer boundary condition; 3-parameter inverse fit (x_core, j_0, T_oven_eff); test whether main-bake RMSE drops below the M9 Stefan baseline (median 7.5 deg C) when the model has both correct physics class AND correct boundary conditions (radiative not Dirichlet).
actual_outcome: Zurcher 2014 two-state model implemented; forward solver reproduces Figs 4 and 6 qualitatively. Real-CSV inverse fits 5-7x WORSE than M9 Stefan (main-bake RMSE 35-38 deg C across all 7 fixtures vs M9's 6-11 deg C). Free parameters all hit lower bounds (j_0 = 0.005, T_oven_eff = 350 K) — optimizer compensating for a centre-overheat bug in Zurcher's eq 6 at the user's coarse-graining. Zurcher himself flags this regime as unreliable for centre temperature inference. CONFIRM-information-limit: 3 published model classes have now failed below 6 deg C main-bake RMSE; in-dough thermometry alone does not carry enough information. Method 4 (loaf-thickness metadata) is the only path forward.
success_metric_result: 29/29 Bellona tests pass; forward solver reproduces Zurcher Figs 4-6; real-CSV main-bake RMSE 5-7x worse than M9; all free parameters at boundaries (optimizer artefact); verdict CONFIRM-information-limit.

adopt: Cite the model author's own warnings — Zurcher explicitly says 'temperature at the center is an unreliable indicator' for this regime. Should have read that flag before implementing the inverse
avoid: Treating a literature model as right by default — Zurcher's eq 6 + 1mm coarse-graining produces a 6x-too-fast centre rise; literature solutions don't always survive numerical implementation
